failure_modes: Blend too high (C011) removes the static anchor and can displace surrounding coordinates along a non-monotone observed-node teacher whose contrast functions change sign and rate across the window.
The observed-node teacher is only admissible as interpolation over the observed support; any extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.5] is unsupported and could degrade the primary affinity objective.
No decoded terminal labels or final-affinity outcome data were supplied, so the expected advantage is inferred from coordinate contrasts and cannot be confirmed as final affinity benefit.
The shape second-moment contrasts are coordinate rewards, not physical interaction energies or affinity-head derivatives; treating them as such would be an unsupported interpretation.
rationale: D1.2: The registered temporal_teacher recipe (C009-C011) keeps the same static detached teachers and the same shared FLOWR endpoint; it changes only the blend weight between the static coordinate reward and the observed-node teacher reward, i.e. it is a dose on a coordinate reward, not a velocity target and not a spatial gradient of a temporal derivative. The observed contrast functions are non-monotone with sign changes and no accepted polynomial fit (E2e106e083189d150, E03ad082bb04f4f9c, Eace79c1f0f54c9d1), so a constant static rule is not supported over the observed support, while the time-conditioned alternative is admissible only as observed-node interpolation. D4.1: Against the incumbent (teacher_neighbors=4, static reward, pointcloud_delta_A=1.0), the defensible expected advantage is the time-conditioned blend rather than a stationary coordinate target, because the endpoint contrasts that carry the signal are the shape second-moment contrasts (E3114d60bf4cd5720, Ecbb36ef90768cba0, Efd40af47235b6ecf) and the centroid components are mostly null after multiplicity adjustment. C010 (temporal_teacher_blend=0.5) is chosen over C009 and C011 as the bounded midpoint: it retains half the incumbent static reward, so the shared learned support is preserved and the change is a dose, not a replacement of teacher coordinates or regional attention. D4.2: Predicted failure response: if the blend is pushed to 1.0 (C011), the static anchor is removed and the non-monotone observed-node teacher can drive unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates, since the observed contrast functions change sign and rate across the window and extrapolation is disallowed; the 0.5 blend bounds that displacement while keeping the affinity-first priority. No temperature edit is proposed; mixture_temperature and teacher_endpoint_temperature_A2 remain at their fixed values.
